claim.pdf_says: Each successive element within that dimension of the table is referenced by occurrence numbers of 2, 3, ... . The highest permissible occurrence number for any given dimension of a fixed-capacity or occurs-depending table is the maximum number of occurrences of the item as specified in the associated OCCURS clause.
claim.markdown_says:
Each successive element within that dimension of the table is referenced by occurrence numbers of 2, 3, . . . The highest permissible

   occurrence number for any given dimension of a fixed-capacity or occurs-depending table is the maximum\
   number of occurrences of the item as specified in the associated OCCURS clause.
claim.why_it_matters: General rule 2 of 8.4.1.2.3 is one paragraph in the PDF; the markdown breaks it mid-sentence with a blank line and hard line breaks, so the rest of the rule (the dynamic-capacity limit and the EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT condition) renders as a separate indented paragraph detached from rule 2. No words are lost.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page (p.98 of the 2014 PDF, page 122) shows general rule 2 of 8.4.1.2.3 as one paragraph. The markdown carries every word of it in order: the blank line after 'The highest permissible' and the hard line breaks only change line wrapping. The continuation is indented three spaces under '2\)', so Markdown still renders it inside list item 2, not as a separate rule. The claim itself says no words are lost. The '...' vs '. . .' difference is glyph spacing. Nothing in the rule's meaning changes, so this is a formatting difference and not a content discrepancy.
